title: Theo and the Parish
premise: Juniper Pemberton, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, takes what looks like a routine missing-person claim: Theo Marsh, a quiet organist from the parish of St. Aldwyn's, vanished three weeks ago. But the diary Juniper recovers keeps being written after his disappearance, and its entries describe her own arrival in town before she ever arrived. As the parish's anniversary dinner approaches, Juniper realizes Theo faked his death to escape a decades-old crime recorded in the church's restoration ledger—a ledger hidden in plain sight as hymn numbers on the noticeboard—and that someone in the congregation is killing to keep it buried. In the end, Juniper decodes the ledger during the anniversary toast, exposes the warden who murdered to protect the parish's name, and must choose between turning in Theo for insurance fraud or letting the man who saved her life stay invisible.
about_author: Beatrix Sterling is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living. She writes mysteries from a converted vestry on the Yorkshire coast, where the church bells still ring on Sundays.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Juniper Pemberton accepts the Marsh missing-person file from Meridian Mutual, noting the payout hinges on proof of death. POV: Juniper. She arrives in St. Aldwyn's rain-soaked high street, memorizing faces out of habit. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking a restlessness she can't name.

chapters.title: A Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper interviews the vicar, Mrs. Halloway the postmistress, and churchwarden Edmund Voss, cataloguing contradictions in their accounts of Theo. POV: Juniper. Everyone describes him kindly and vaguely, like a man already erased. Emotional beat: her first unease—the village remembers too well, and too identically.

chapters.title: The Organ Loft
chapters.summary: Searching Theo's cottage above the vestry, Juniper finds sheet music annotated with dates that don't match services, and a locked drawer forced open by someone else. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt sharpening into something personal—Theo was careful, and careful men don't simply vanish.

chapters.title: Diary of a Living Man
chapters.summary: Juniper locates Theo's diary hidden in the organ bench. The final entry is dated nine days after his disappearance. POV: Juniper, with diary excerpts interleaved. The entry mentions 'the investigator with the perfect memory.' Emotional beat: cold dread—she was expected.

chapters.title: Hymn Numbers
chapters.summary: Juniper notices the noticeboard's hymn selections repeat in impossible patterns and photographs every board in the parish. POV: Juniper. Voss watches her from the churchyard gate. Emotional beat: suspicion crystallizing—the parish communicates in code because it has something to hide.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Weighs
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: 1979, through the diary's earlier entries, young Theo witnessed a break-in at the restoration fund—money meant for the roof diverted by founding families. POV: alternating Theo (diary) and Juniper. Emotional beat: sympathy blooming; the victim became a witness became a fugitive.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: Juniper receives an unexpected invitation to the parish's sesquicentennial anniversary dinner, hand-delivered by Voss himself. POV: Juniper. She accepts against instinct. Emotional beat: the sense of walking into a trap she can't refuse, and the strange comfort of being wanted somewhere.

chapters.title: The Man in the Gallery
chapters.summary: During evening service, Juniper spots a figure in the organ gallery who moves like Theo. He leaves a note under her pew: 'Stop looking. They'll bury you with me.' POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: fear braided with fascination—her first direct contact with the missing man.

chapters.title: Photographic
chapters.summary: Juniper reconstructs the hymn-number sequences from memory across six months of noticeboards, mapping them to dates in the diary. POV: Juniper. The pattern points to a second ledger, physical and hidden. Emotional beat: the intoxication of her gift finally mattering, and its loneliness.

chapters.title: Mrs. Halloway's Confession
chapters.summary: The elderly postmistress admits she has been posting letters for Theo since his disappearance—he's alive, hiding in the coastguard station. She begs Juniper not to report him. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: complicity offered; the first crack in her duty-first identity.

chapters.title: Voss's Version
chapters.summary: Voss confronts Juniper with her own file: Meridian Mutual once investigated the 1979 theft and closed it wrong, ruining an innocent man—her own firm's stain. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case is about her employer's sin as much as Theo's flight.

chapters.title: The Coastguard Station
chapters.summary: Juniper meets Theo face to face. He explains he staged his death when someone ransacked his cottage, and that the real ledger records forty years of hush money paid by parish founders. POV: alternating Juniper and Theo. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two people who survive by not being seen, seeing each other.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: The village buzzes with dinner preparations while Juniper narrows the ledger's location: the church's foundation stone, opened only during centenary ceremonies. POV: Juniper. Someone searches her room. Emotional beat: closing walls; the killer knows how close she is.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Juniper exhumes records showing the man officially buried as Theo's father died under circumstances matching the 1979 theft—the first murder was never investigated. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger; the price of survival paid a generation early.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Theo asks Juniper to walk away before the dinner; she realizes she's fallen for him and that reporting him would destroy him. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the central wound—her flawless record versus the first person worth blemishing it for.

chapters.title: The Second Death
chapters.summary: Mrs. Halloway is found dead, her letters stolen, staged as an accident. POV: Juniper. The killer is inside the dinner committee. Emotional beat: rage and guilt—her investigation painted a target on the one person who helped her.

chapters.title: Decoding the Toast
chapters.summary: Juniper realizes the anniversary toast follows the same numerical structure as the hymn codes—the ceremony itself is the key that opens the foundation stone. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: grim clarity; the parish will reveal its own crime in front of everyone.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: At the dinner, Juniper plays along with the toasts while tracking Voss, whose rehearsed speech contains the ledger's opening sequence verbatim. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: high-wire tension beneath candlelight and clinking glasses.

chapters.title: Foundation Stone
chapters.summary: After midnight, Juniper and Theo open the stone and recover the ledger naming Voss's father and the living Voss as keepers of the fraud—and of both deaths. POV: alternating. Voss catches them inside the crypt. Emotional beat: trapped with the truth and the man willing to kill for it.

chapters.title: Bells at Midnight
chapters.summary: Voss attacks; Theo rings the bells to summon the village, sacrificing his invisibility. Juniper uses her memory of Voss's own words to corner him into confession before witnesses. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: climax—duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Voss is arrested; the parish reels. Juniper files her report but omits the staged death, classifying the policy as withdrawn rather than fraudulent. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: quiet cost—her first falsified record, and no regret she can admit to.

chapters.title: A New Entry
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Juniper returns to St. Aldwyn's, resigning from Meridian Mutual. Theo, publicly 'returned' with a plausible story, begins a new diary. Its first entry names her. POV: alternating Juniper and Theo. Emotional beat: resolution—two people who chose each other over the versions of themselves that survived.
